name: Spondyloepiphyseal Dysplasia, Kimberley Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Spondyloepiphyseal Dysplasia, Kimberley Type

criteria.description: Short stature with disproportionate shortening of the trunk and limbs
Radiographic evidence of epiphyseal and vertebral abnormalities including platyspondyly and delayed ossification
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with Kimberley type SED (e.g., COL2A1 mutations)
Presence of characteristic facial dysmorphism and joint stiffness

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation and radiological findings consistent with SED Kimberley type; genetic confirmation supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can aid in confirmation but diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiological.

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific biochemical markers
imaging: X-rays showing platyspondyly, delayed epiphyseal ossification, and vertebral abnormalities
MRI may reveal spinal cord compression in advanced cases
other: Clinical assessment of disproportionate short stature and joint mobility

distinguishingFeatures: More severe dwarfism with earlier onset
Distinct radiological patterns without Kimberley type features
Disproportionate short-limb dwarfism rather than short trunk
Characteristic facial features and genetic mutation in FGFR3

redFlags: Progressive neurological deficits indicating spinal cord compression
Severe respiratory compromise due to thoracic deformities
Rapidly worsening joint contractures or severe osteoarthritis in childhood
references: Orphanet: Spondyloepiphyseal Dysplasia, Kimberley Type - ORPHA:93283
Superti-Furga A, Unger S. Nosology and classification of genetic skeletal disorders: 2019 revision. Am J Med Genet A. 2019
